stem: What two things decide how serious a risk is?

options.content: How likely it is to happen and how large its impact would be
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: How much the equipment cost and how old it is
options.rationale: Cost and age may matter but they do not define the risk.

options.content: Who wrote the security policy and when
options.rationale: The author of a policy does not decide the seriousness.

options.content: How fast the computer is and how big its disk is
options.rationale: Speed and capacity do not measure risk.

explanation: Risk depends on likelihood and impact.

stem: A school buys insurance to pay for replacement computers if they are stolen. Which risk management technique is this?

options.content: Transfer
options.rationale: Correct: the financial loss is passed to the insurer.

options.content: Avoid
options.rationale: The school still keeps the computers, so the activity is not avoided.

options.content: Accept the risk
options.rationale: The school has taken a step to cover the loss.

options.content: Reduce
options.rationale: Insurance does not make theft less likely.

explanation: Insurance transfers the financial effect of a risk.

stem: A clinic decides not to put its server in a basement room that has flooded before, and places it on an upper floor. Which technique is this?

options.content: Transfer
options.rationale: Nobody else is taking over the loss.

options.content: Accept the risk
options.rationale: The clinic is acting against the risk.

options.content: Insure
options.rationale: Insurance is a form of transfer and is not in this scenario.

options.content: Avoid
options.rationale: Correct: the risky location is not used.

explanation: Avoiding a risk removes the cause of the risk.

stem: What does an incremental backup copy?

options.content: Everything on the disk every time
options.rationale: That is a full backup.

options.content: Only the operating system
options.rationale: An incremental backup is not limited to the operating system.

options.content: Only the data that has changed since the last backup
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: Only the files that are larger than one gigabyte in size
options.rationale: File size is not the rule.

explanation: Incremental backups save time and storage.

stem: Which alternative site recovers fastest after a disaster, at the highest cost?

options.content: A warm site
options.rationale: A warm site has equipment but needs data restored.

options.content: A hot site
options.rationale: Correct: it is fully equipped and has up-to-date data.

options.content: A cold site
options.rationale: A cold site has only space and power.

options.content: An off-site tape cabinet
options.rationale: A store of copies is not a site where work can start.

explanation: Hot sites are the fastest and the most expensive.
hints: Which site is already running with current data?

stem: Why should a disaster recovery plan include regular tests of restoring from the backups?

options.content: Restoring tests make the backup files smaller
options.rationale: Testing does not change the size of files.

options.content: A restore test stops malware from entering
options.rationale: Tests do not protect against malware.

options.content: Test restores are required by the warranty of every computer that the school buys
options.rationale: Warranties do not require this.

options.content: A backup that has never been restored may be damaged or incomplete, and staff must know the procedure
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: A tested restore proves that the backup is usable.
hints: How does the school know the backup works?

stem: Which item belongs in an organisation's security policy rather than in the details of its backup schedule?

options.content: The time of day when each night's backup starts and finishes
options.rationale: That is a detail of the backup schedule.

options.content: Rules on what staff may do on the internet (acceptable use)
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The size of each incremental backup
options.rationale: That is a detail of the backup schedule.

options.content: The make of the backup disks
options.rationale: That is a detail of the backup equipment.

explanation: Acceptable use is a policy item.
hints: Which one is about the behaviour of people?

stem: Which organisation is most likely to pay for a hot site?

options.content: A small school that uses its computers only for typing notes and printing
options.rationale: The school can wait several days at little cost.

options.content: A person who keeps holiday photographs on one laptop
options.rationale: The cost of a hot site is far greater than the loss.

options.content: A bank whose customers cannot be served when its systems are down
options.rationale: Correct: the cost of lost service is very high.

options.content: A club that updates a web page once a month
options.rationale: A short outage would cost almost nothing.

explanation: A hot site is worth its cost only when downtime is very expensive.
hints: Compare the cost of a hot site with the cost of downtime.

stem: Accepting a risk means ignoring it without any analysis or plan.
explanation: False. Accepting a risk is a decision made after analysis, when the risk is small or the cost of reducing it is too high; the organisation still keeps a plan.

stem: Match each risk management technique to an example.

right.content: Taking out insurance on the computers
Deciding that the very small risk of a flood needs no extra spending
Not storing patient records on a laptop that leaves the clinic
Installing anti-malware software and training staff

explanation: Each technique deals with the risk in a different way.

stem: Complete the sentences about recovery.

payload.template: A {{blank:a}} backup copies everything, and an {{blank:b}} backup copies only changes. A {{blank:c}} site is the slowest and cheapest alternative site to start work in.

explanation: Full, incremental, cold.

stem: Name the type of alternative site that offers only space, power and network connections, with all the equipment to be brought in.
explanation: A cold site.

stem: A risk has a likelihood of 4 and an impact of 5, each on a scale of 1 to 5. Calculate the risk score using likelihood × impact.
explanation: 4 × 5 = 20, which is in the High band (15 to 25).

stem: A school makes a full backup of 30 GB every Sunday and an incremental backup of 3 GB on each of the other six days. It keeps three weeks of backups. Calculate the total storage needed.
workedSolution:
1. Full backups: 3 × 30 = 90 GB.
2. Incremental backups: 3 weeks × 6 days × 3 GB = 54 GB.
3. Total = 90 + 54 = 144 GB.
hints: Three full backups plus 18 incremental backups.

stem: A shop loses US\$80 of sales for each hour its system is down. A fault stops work for 5 hours and this happens 3 times a year. Calculate the loss in a year.
workedSolution:
1. Loss per fault = 80 × 5 = US\$400.
2. Loss per year = 400 × 3 = US\$1200.
hints: Loss per outage = hourly loss × hours, then multiply by the number of outages.

stem: A school wants to protect its computers against power surges. State two risk management techniques it could use, with an example of each. [4]

points.description: Reduce: fit surge protectors or an uninterruptible power supply
Explanation of how this reduces the damage or downtime
Transfer: insure the equipment so that the insurer pays for damage
Explanation: the financial loss is passed to the insurance company

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Reduce the risk by fitting surge protectors or an uninterruptible power supply so that equipment is not damaged and work continues. Transfer the risk by insuring the equipment, so that the insurance company pays for any damage.

explanation: Any two techniques with examples.
hints: Name each technique and give a school example.

stem: Describe four parts of a disaster recovery plan for a school's computer system. [4]

points.description: A backup schedule saying what is copied and how often
Copies kept off-site or in the cloud
A procedure for restoring the system, which is tested regularly
An alternative site or equipment and named people with roles

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A backup schedule saying what is copied and how often; copies kept off-site or in the cloud; a restore procedure that is tested regularly; and an alternative site or equipment with named people responsible.

explanation: Any four parts of a plan.
hints: Think about what is copied, where it is kept and how it is tested.

stem: State three items that a security policy of a school should contain. [3]

points.description: Acceptable use of computers and the internet
Access control, such as passwords and who may use which system
Incident response or staff training, or data handling

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Rules on acceptable use of computers and the internet, rules on access control and passwords, and how to report and respond to an incident.

explanation: Any three policy items.

stem: A school considers keeping its backups with a cloud service. Evaluate this choice. [4]

points.description: Advantage: the copy is off-site and survives fire, flood or theft at the school
Advantage: backups can be automatic and restored from anywhere with a connection
Disadvantage: it needs a reliable and affordable internet connection, which may be slow or costly
Disadvantage: the data is held by another company, so privacy and security must be agreed

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The copy is off-site, so it survives fire or theft, and backups can be automatic and restored from anywhere. However, it needs a reliable and affordable internet connection and the data is held by another company, so privacy and security have to be agreed.

explanation: Two advantages and two disadvantages.
hints: Give two advantages and two disadvantages.

stem:
A school in Mutare scores five risks. Each likelihood and impact is on a scale of 1 to 5.

| Risk | Likelihood (1-5) | Impact (1-5) |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Ransomware attack | 3 | 5 |
| Lightning strike on the school | 2 | 4 |
| Learner unplugging cables | 5 | 1 |
| Theft of a tablet | 4 | 3 |
| Failure of the hard disk | 3 | 4 |

The score is likelihood × impact. A score of 1 to 5 is Low, 6 to 12 is Medium and 15 to 25 is High.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the score for the ransomware attack.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the level (Low, Medium or High) of the risk of a lightning strike.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Which risk has the lowest score?

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: The school decides to insure the tablets and to install anti-malware software. Name the technique used in each case.

points.description: Insuring the tablets: transfer
Installing anti-malware software: reduce
The technique is chosen by what it does to the risk (passes the loss on, or lowers the likelihood or impact)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Insuring the tablets is transfer. Installing anti-malware software is reduce, because it makes a malware attack less likely.

explanation: The scores are Ransomware attack: 15, Lightning strike on the school: 8, Learner unplugging cables: 5, Theft of a tablet: 12, Failure of the hard disk: 12.
hints: Score = likelihood × impact. Use the bands in the lesson: Low 1 to 5, Medium 6 to 12, High 15 to 25.

stem: A college in Gweru makes a full backup of 30 GB every Sunday and an incremental backup of 3 GB on each of the other six days. It keeps three weeks of backups. Use 1 GB = 1024 MB.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the storage needed for the three weeks of backups.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: The disk fails on Wednesday morning. Calculate how much data must be restored: the last full backup and the incrementals taken since.
parts.workedSolution:
1. Sunday full backup = 30 GB.
2. Monday and Tuesday incrementals = 2 × 3 = 6 GB.
3. Total = 36 GB.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Restoring runs at 150 MB per second. Calculate the time in seconds to restore the data in (b). Give your answer to the nearest second.
parts.workedSolution:
1. 36 × 1024 = 36864 MB.
2. 36864 ÷ 150 = 245.76 seconds, or 246 to the nearest second.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Give one reason for using incremental backups on six days and a full backup only once a week.

points.description: An incremental backup copies only changed data, so it is quicker
It uses much less storage than copying everything every day

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: An incremental backup copies only changed data, so it is quicker and uses much less storage than a full backup every day.

explanation: Storage is 144 GB. A restore on Wednesday needs 36 GB and takes 245.76 seconds at 150 MB per second.
hints: Add three full backups and eighteen incrementals.
Restore needs the last full backup and the incrementals since it.

stem: A clinic in Hwange is offered insurance for its laptops. The premium is US\$90 a year. A theft that would cost US\$450 to put right happens on average once every 3 years.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the average loss per year from theft.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: State the risk management technique that insurance is, and say whether it is worth buying.

points.description: Transfer
It is worth buying because the average yearly loss (US\$150) is more than the premium (US\$90)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Transfer. It is worth buying because the average loss of US\$150 a year is more than the premium of US\$90.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Suggest a second measure that reduces the likelihood of theft.

points.description: A physical measure such as a lockable cabinet, cable lock or a locked room
Explanation of how it makes theft harder

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A cable lock or lockable cabinet makes the laptops harder to remove.

explanation: The expected yearly loss is US\$150, more than the premium of US\$90, so insurance is worth it.
hints: Compare the yearly loss with the yearly cost.
